Hi Nathan — thanks for the forecast and the clear questions. Short answers up front, then details below.

TL;DR:
- We support both quarterly and annual true-ups. Quarterly is available for committed customers; credits are issued as invoice credits (make-goods) within the following billing cycle.
- Make-goods: if actual usage < committed minimum, we discount billed amount down to the commit level for the period (customer owes the commit), but if customer overpays we issue a credit. If usage < committed and customer wants to reduce future commits, we can include a pro-rated true-down at renewal with approval.
- Reporting: we provide per-API-key per-day token breakdowns and signed usage exports for audit.

Details / Options we typically offer:
1) Quarterly true-up (recommended for variable ramps)
   - Commit is set as monthly average for the quarter.
   - At quarter end we compare actual tokens to committed tokens.
   - If actual >= commit: excess billed at standard per-token rate (no clawback).
   - If actual < commit: customer is credited the delta as an invoice credit (make-good) OR the shortfall can be carried forward toward next quarter if both parties opt in.
   - Credits appear on the next invoice within 30 days after reconciliation.

2) Annual true-up (standard, less operational overhead)
   - Single reconciliation at year-end. Make-goods applied as credits on renewal invoice.

3) Commit flex (hybrid)
   - We can write a short addendum: quarterly reconciliation but an annual re-baseline for next year’s commit with pro-rating. Good for customers with seasonal spikes.

4) Discounting and tiers
   - Discounts are applied to the committed per-token price. We can tier discounts by commit band (e.g., 5% @ 1M tokens/mo, 10% @ 5M tokens/mo).
   - For sales exceptions (e.g., >10% discount), we need approval from Sales Ops — I’ve CC'd Marissa to expedite.

Attachments included: redwood_pricing_v3.pdf (pricing bands and definitions), commit_schedule.xlsx (example quarterly true-up schedule).

If you prefer, I can propose a sample clause for the SOW that spells out\"make-good\" timing and caps.

Thanks — happy to sync for 30 minutes tomorrow if useful.
